contexts.text: Where there is gold. And the gold of that land is good ()... Gold = good... The reason gold is mentioned twice, is that it = the good of love, and the good of faith from love... Such is the celestial man. Coro 27.
That the good of wisdom or of love is signified and represented by gold. Illustrated.
Idols which they ornament with gold (), that is, falsities with seeming good.
For brass gold () = for natural good celestial good. AC 1551:2. AE 176:3.
The Most Ancients compared... man's... inmost Celestial to gold; his lower Celestial to brass... Illustrated.
Gold () = love to the Lord.

Gold, frankincense, and myrrh = celestial, spiritual, and natural good. DSS 23:3. AR 277:end. AE 324:10. AE 491:5. ( = celestial love, spiritual love, and these loves in the Natural. AC 4262:3.) Compare AC 9293:3. AC 10252:5.
Rays of golden flame.
The Most Ancients compared... the inmost or celestial goods, which are of love to the Lord, to gold.
The Golden Age was the time of the Most Ancient Church, which was a celestial man.
The like is signified by the head of Nebuchadnezzar's statue being of good gold. AC 2162:3.
Gold () = the Knowledges of celestial things. Illustrated. AC 3240:6. ( = the good of love. AE 195:7.)
The gold of the nations () = evils. AC 9193:3.
Cupidities are gods of gold ().
And in gold () = goods from truths; (for) gold = celestial good, or the good of wisdom and love. The reason it here = goods from truths. Explained.
Atmospheres flaming as with gold.
(Gold like clear glass = truths pellucid from good.)
Gold = the good of love. References. AC 3862:6. AC 6135:end. AE 62. AE 62:end. AE 65. AE 242:9, Illustrated.
Gold of Uphaz () = the good of wisdom which is from love.
Its head of gold = the first state of the Church, which was celestial, because of love to the Lord.
Gold and incense = goods and truths.
The vessels of gold and silver () = the Knowledges of good and truth, which were profaned. AC 8932:7.
A pendant of gold () = Divine good; because the Lord is treated of.
Silver and gold () = truths in general (as distinguished from truths in special).
The doctrinal things of good are gold ().
Gold, silver, etc., as spoil, = truths falsified.
Earrings of gold () = the things which are of simple good.
If gold is mentioned in the Word, there is meant the good of love and of wisdom. AC 8988:5.
Affections of good are represented by veins of golden flame.
Gold = celestial good. AC 6432:2. HH 115:end. TCR 609. AE 70:2.
The falsity which they veil over with holiness is the cup of gold ().
The tongue of gold, etc. () = semblances of falsity.
A chain of gold () = conjunction through good.
To buy gold () = to procure and appropriate good. AC 9960:7.
Gold = celestial and spiritual good. References.
Adorned with gold and silver () = with celestial and spiritual good and truth.
They called those times the Golden Age when there was innocence and integrity, and when everyone lid good from good, and justice from justice. AC 8118.

When there is speech in a higher Heaven about good, what is golden appears with those who are in the First Heaven... sometimes so, that not only the walls of the chambers where they dwell sparkle with gold and silver, but also the very atmosphere. Moreover, with the Angels of the First Heaven, who are in good from good, there appear tables of gold, candelabra of gold, and many other things.
How should we steal... silver or gold? () = why should we claim for ourselves truth and good...?
The golden candlesticks = the truths of good.
Girt about at the paps with a golden girdle = the good of love.
Golden crowns upon their heads () = the goods of wisdom.
Vessels of gold () = scientifics of good. AC 7770.
The gold with which the cherubs and palms were covered over () = the good of love, which reigns universally in the Heavens.

Gods of silver, and gods of gold () = things which in external form appear to be truths and goods, but in the internal are falsities and evils... Gold, in the opposite sense, = evil. Illustrated. AC 9146:2.
To cover over with gold () = to make them appear good in the external form. Illustrated.
The gold (which is sanctified by the temple) = the good which is from the Lord.
Gold = the good which is from the Divine, thus which is from the Word.
Silver and gold = falsities from evil.
The first state of the Church as to the reception of the truth proceeding from the Lord is gold (); because by gold is signified celestial good, which is the good of love to the Lord. AE 176:2.
Idols of gold = evils of doctrine.
Gold and silver () = internal good and truth in general.
Thou shalt overlay it with pure gold () = that all these things are to be founded on good. AC 10194.
Without and within there was gold, by which is also signified good, but such good as appears before the sense, thus relatively external good.
A rim of gold () = a bounding from good lest they should be approached and injured by evils.
Four rings of gold () = Divine truth conjoined with Divine good, which is round about on all sides.
Thou shalt overlay them with gold () = good on all sides.
Thou shalt make a mercy-seat of pure gold () = the hearing and reception of all things of worship from the good of love.
Of solid gold thou shalt make them () = a representative of good. Gold = the good of love.

Thou shalt overlay it with [pure] gold () = a representative of that good from mercy. To overlay with gold = a representative of good; for gold = the good of love; and therefore where that good was introduced it was represented by gold.
Of pure gold () = from celestial good.
As this Divine truth exists from the Divine good, the candlestick was of gold. Explained.
One solid thing of pure gold () = what is complete and perfect, because from the same good.
Of pure gold () = also from good.

A talent of pure gold () = one good from which are all things... As good must be in all things which are produced and derived; and as therefore celestial good must be in spiritual goods, and from them in scientifics, it is said that the candlestick shall be made solid of pure gold; and that the shaft, the branch, the bowls, the pomegranates, and the flowers, shall be made of it...

They shall take gold () = the good which reigns universally; (for) gold = the good of love... and that this reigns universally, is signified by the gold being interwoven everywhere in the ephod... The gold was interwoven everywhere for this reason, that by the garments of Aaron was represented the Spiritual Heaven, and good reigns in that Heaven, as well as in the other Heavens... AC 9834.
In ouches of gold () = existence and subsistence from good. Explained.
The case with good and truth is the same as with the gold whereby a precious stone is enclosed; for good is like soil, and truths are like the seeds in it...
Two little chains of pure gold () = the coherence with the good of the whole Kingdom... It is said pure gold, because good from the Divine is signified.
They shall be inclosed in gold in their fillings () = that each and all things in general and in particular shall proceed from the good which is of love from the Lord to the Lord. Explained.

Of pure gold () = through celestial good. Gold = the good of love... And as it is said pure gold, it is celestial good which is meant; for there is celestial good and spiritual good, and each of them internal and external... All these goods are called gold, and are distinguished by gold from Uphaz, from Ophir, from Sheba and Havillah, and also from Tarshish; (which = celestial good, spiritual good, the good of Knowledges, and scientific good respectively). Illustrated.
By putting the two plattings of gold on the two rings () is signified the method of the indissoluble conjunction of good with the Divine sphere.
Bells of gold () = all things of doctrine and worship from good passing to those who are of the Church.
A plate of pure gold () = enlightenment from the Divine good of the Lord. Explained.
Goods and truths from self and not from the Lord are signified by gold, silver, and brass in their girdles ().
Gold = the good which is of wisdom.
Because the first state of the Church was a state of good of love to the Lord it is said that its head was of gold.
Thou shalt overlay it with pure gold () = a representative of all things of worship from good.
A border of gold round about () = a bounding from good to prevent their being approached and injured by evils. Explained.
Two rings of gold for it from beneath the border () = the sphere of Divine good, by which there is conjunction and preservation.
To buy gold purified in the fire = to acquire genuine good from the Lord.
With the Angels all things appear as it were refulgent with gold, silver, and precious stones, and this because they are in the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of good. AE 118:end.
To make in gold, in silver, and in brass () = to represent goods and truths interior and exterior which are of the understanding from the will... Gold = interior good...

Pluck the earrings of gold from the ears... () = the extraction of such things from the sense of the letter as favour external loves and the principles thence derived... Gold = the good of love; here, the delight of external loves.
Gold = good in general. References.
They have made for themselves gods of gold () = they worship infernal delight. Gold = the delight of external loves, thus infernal delight.
Idols of gold = the worship of evil in both doctrine and life; thus they = worship the worst of all.
The palaces of Heaven shone above as if of pure gold... HH 361.
Fruits as of gold. CL 13.
Gold like pure glass = the good of love, from which doctrine... is pellucent. NJHD 1.
Uses themselves are thus refulgent in Heaven; the good of use as gold, and the truth of use as silver.
The Jews want to know the arcana of the Word, when it is said that they are about gold.
In the bosom of the earth... are minerals impregnated with gold, silver, and iron; from the exhalations stored up in the earth, gold derives its own element, silver its, and iron its.
Goods from God, and from self, may be compared to gold. (And to gilding.) Explained.
Haemorrhoids of gold () = natural loves purified and made good. Mice of gold = the vastation of the Church taken away by means of good.

Seven golden candlesticks () = the New Church, which will be in enlightenment by the Lord from the Word... The candlesticks were seen to be golden, because gold = good; and every Church is a Church from the good which is formed through truths. AE 62.
Girt about at the paps with a golden girdle () = the proceeding and at the same time conjoining Divine, which is Divine good. AE 65.

I counsel thee to buy of Me gold tried in the fire, that thou mayest be rich () = admonition to acquire from the Lord through the Word the good of love, that they may be wise... Gold = good; and gold tried in the fire, the good of celestial love. ( = genuine good. AE 242.)
The reason gold = good, is that the metals in their order = such things as are of good and truth; gold, celestial and spiritual good; silver, the truth of these loves...
By the Golden Age they meant the first time, when the good of celestial love reigned. Celestial love is love to the Lord from the Lord; and from this love they then had wisdom.
They had upon their heads golden crowns () = the things which are of wisdom from love... Gold = the good of love. AR 432. See AE 272, AE 553. AE 907.
The gold of Sheba = wisdom thence. TCR 706:5.
Gold and precious stone () = Divine good and truth spiritual. AR 726, Explained. AR 772:2.
The good and truth with the Angels of the Spiritual Kingdom are signified by gold and precious stone.
A golden reed to measure the city... () = that there is given by the Lord to those who are in the good of love the faculty of understanding and knowing the quality of the Lord's New Church...
The city was pure gold like unto pure glass () = that thence everything of that Church is the good of love flowing in together with light out of Heaven from the Lord. AR 917.
As there is no good of love solitary, or abstracted from the truths of wisdom... it is here described as pure gold like unto pure glass...

The reason gold = the good of love, is that the metals... correspond; gold, to the good of love; silver, to the truths of wisdom; copper or brass, to the good of charity; and iron, to the truths of faith. Illustrated.
The palace was roofed with plates of gold. Its window posts were of gold.
A high pyramid of gold in the middle of the table.
I saw their tabernacle as it were overlaid with gold. (This appearance was caused by the flaming light.)
A pomegranate with seeds of gold.
All their house furniture was refulgent with gold...
[155a]. A golden shower.
A dove with a crown of gold.
The atmosphere there appears golden...
Little grains of gold magnified to look like coins.
Gold = internal good.
The Jews say that interiorly in the Word there is nothing but gold.
(Self-confidence appearing as gold; but filthy within.)
A slight sprinkling of golden dust, which signifies something of the affection of good.
Clothed in gilded garments.
(A dream about gold.)
On a golden and a silver heart.
Gold = the good of the internal man. Illustrated.
Gold in thy treasures () = the Knowledges of good.
Their silver and their gold with them = the Knowledges of truth and good they have.
The gold of Sheba = ... the good of love...
The queen at his right hand in the best gold of Ophir () = the Lord's Celestial Kingdom which is in the good of love.
Gold, in the opposite, = the evil of the love of self. Illustrated.
Gold = the good which is from the Lord.
Feathers with yellowness of gold = the spiritual good from which are these truths.
The gold and incense which they shall bring = worship from spiritual good which is from celestial good.
The gold of Sheba = the good of charity. AE 329:18.
The pure gold the plate was made of = the good of celestial love.
A golden censer = spiritual good from celestial good, Explained.
The golden altar = the Heaven where is spiritual good.
Gold and silver = the goods and truths of the Internal Church.
Silver from Tarshish, and gold from Uphaz () = appearing in the external form as truth and good.
The head of gold = the Most Ancient Church...
Gold from Uphaz = the good of the Word in the sense of the letter. AE 587:6.
Gold = spiritual good.
A golden idol = (false doctrine confirmed by the spiritual good of the Word.)
Covered over with gold = that it appears as good in the external form.
Adorned with gold and silver = the love of good and truth...
More to be desired are they than gold, and than much fine gold... Gold = celestial good; and fine gold, spiritual good.
Their silver and gold () = the falsities and evils of the religion which is from Own intelligence and Own will.
To make gold a hope, and to say. Pure gold, my trust () = that he did not confide in himself, by believing that there is anything of good from self.
Silver and gold = the truths and goods of the Church; and, in the opposite sense, its evils and falsities.
Gold = evils.
The best gold of Ophir- = the good of love to the Lord.
The gold and silver (of Jericho) = the Knowledges of spiritual good and truth.
They made images of haemorrhoids and mice of gold... because gold = the good of love, which heals and purifies from falsities and evils...
Silver and gold, here, = what is false and evil. AE 827:5.
Everything true and good in general is signified by silver and gold.
Gold is given (to those beneath the Heavens) from the Third Heaven; because... gold corresponds to celestial good.
Her clothing of interweavings of gold () = investing truths formed from the good of love.
Gold = spiritual good.
A cup of gold () = falsity destroying good.
The gold (in the head of the statue) = the good of love to the Lord.
The metals gold, silver, copper, and iron correspond respectively, to celestial good, spiritual truth, natural good, and natural truth.
The gold of Ophir = good.

Merchandize of gold and silver () = the goods and truths of the Word, of doctrine, and of the Church, in general, all profaned by them; thus all the evils and falsities in general from which they derive gain.
Fruits and seeds in the Inmost Heaven of pure gold; in the Middle Heaven of silver; and in the Lowest Heaven, of copper.
Golden things correspond to the affections of the Angels of the Third Heaven...
The spiritual state of the Church as to the good of love is described by gold.
